defaults.time: timeoutMs 10,000 ms wall clock per exec or wait call (clamp 100-60,000), shared by worker preparation, guest work and inline tool waits; approval waits pause it. Pending tool calls can instead return status 'waiting' for a later wait with a fresh budget (src/agents/code-mode-runtime.ts:110; docs/tools/code-mode/configuration.md).
defaults.output: maxOutputBytes 64 KiB shared by output entries, value and error across waits (clamp 1 KiB-10 MiB); over the cap a {truncated, omittedBytes, guidance, prefix} marker replaces the item. Console: each string clipped to 512 UTF-16 units with '…[truncated]', 16,384 units per cell then '[console output truncated]' (code-mode-runtime.ts:112; code-mode-controller-source.ts:101-115; code-mode-json.ts:93). A trailing expression returns null; only `return` sets the value.
defaults.tool_calls: maxPendingToolCalls 16 in flight (clamp 1-128); further calls queue in the guest, up to 128 queued ordinary calls (code-mode-runtime.ts:114; code-mode-controller-source.ts:12, :227-230; code-mode-worker-types.ts:10). No per-exec total call cap was found on the exec path: 40 calls ran. Headless scripts default to 5 calls (code-mode-runtime.ts:26).
defaults.memory: memoryLimitBytes 64 MiB as the QuickJS engine memory limit (clamp 1 MiB-1 GiB), fixed maxStackSize; serialized suspended state capped by maxSnapshotBytes 10 MiB (code-mode.worker.ts:264-265; code-mode-runtime.ts:111-113). Not a Gateway RSS limit.

source_notes.finding: Every catalog-eligible tool becomes an async global function (callableName) plus a callable handle; bindings come from createCodeModeCatalogBindings. The model sees a bounded quick index of `name input -> output` hints built from JSON Schema, capped at 8,000 chars, and TypeScript-style declarations through API.list/API.read. Executable cells are plain JavaScript; TypeScript syntax and require/import are rejected before execution.

Hidden catalog, searched on demand: only exec and wait (plus required direct-only tools) are model-visible (telemetry visibleTools [exec, wait] in every result). Tools past the 8,000-char index are reachable through catalog.search(query) (BM25 lexical index, default 8 results, max 50) and handle.describe(). Scales past 100 tools without putting every schema in the prompt.

Guest calls go through the controller's request() into a host callback that carries only strings (method, JSON args, id, stack); the host runs the call through runtime.callExactValue, the same tool execution path as normal turns (policy, approvals, before_tool_call hooks). Replies are queued on the host and pulled by the guest (__openclawSettleBridge). QuickJS: host functions installed with vm.newFunction in the worker; the guest keeps a serializable snapshot while suspended.

QuickJS compiled to WASM/WASI (quickjs-wasi 3.6.3, bundled; TextEncoder/TextDecoder come from the encoding.so extension inside the same WASM heap), in a worker thread from a shared WorkerTaskPool. No WASI preopens or env are given, so no ambient fs, network, subprocess or environment. memoryLimit = memoryLimitBytes, fixed maxStackSize, and an interruptHandler that checks the wall-clock deadline. The docs claim 'hardened guest isolation' with 'no ambient host access', which matches the probes: guest errors are guest-realm (e.constructor === RangeError), every Function-constructor path returns undefined for process.

The model gets one JSON document: status, telemetry, ordered output entries (text(), json(), console.*) and the returned value or error. Over-budget items become an explicit truncation marker with the original JSON prefix and omittedBytes, not a silent cut. Console strings are clipped to 512 units each.

All limits come from tools.codeMode (global or per agent) and are clamped in resolveCodeModeConfig: timeoutMs 10 s (100 ms-60 s), memoryLimitBytes 64 MiB (1 MiB-1 GiB), maxOutputBytes 64 KiB, maxSnapshotBytes 10 MiB, maxPendingToolCalls 16, snapshotTtlSeconds 900. For QuickJS, memoryLimitBytes is the engine heap limit and timeoutMs drives the interrupt handler; snapshots are capped by maxSnapshotBytes.

Each exec gets a fresh context (globals never carry over), confirmed by P8. Workers are pooled and reused only when cells run inside the Gateway's bound resource host; without it every Node cell starts a new worker (about 200 ms). There is opt-in persistence: store(key, value)/load(key) keep small JSON values per session across cells and restarts, but only for a session-bound run (P8 #3 fails in this harness). A suspended cell (status 'waiting') keeps a serialized VM snapshot for wait.

source_notes.finding: Guest errors return status failed with code internal_error and `Name: message` plus stack frames rewritten to openclaw-code-mode:user.js:line:col (user line numbers, wrapper removed); error text is bounded to 16,384 units. Parse errors are reported before execution with line and column. A runtime `ReferenceError: process|require|module is not defined` is rewritten into the generic 'module access is disabled' invalid_input message. Tool errors are catchable in guest code and are redacted (input shown as [redacted]).

With tools.codeMode absent, activation is 'auto': Code Mode engages automatically for catalog-preferred models (for example claude-opus-5-5, gpt-5.6, gemini-3.5-flash) with the Node executor unless executor: 'quickjs' is set. Credentials stay host-side: tools run in the Gateway with their normal auth, and the guest only receives JSON results. The lexical module check (code-mode-source.ts:226) is a usability guard, not a security control: it blocks the literal require()/import() but not Function-constructor paths.

surprises: QuickJS is opt-in: the default executor is Node (not a security boundary), and 'auto' activation engages Code Mode for preferred models without selecting QuickJS. Only an explicit executor: 'quickjs' gets this isolation.

The plugin's register() is empty; selection works through the manifest's codeModeExecutors contract and a public-surface module load, and an explicit executor choice bypasses plugins.allow for this bundled plugin (src/plugins/code-mode-executor.ts:15-66).
A runtime 'process is not defined' is reported as invalid_input 'code mode module access is disabled.' (shorter text than the Node executor's), which hides the real ReferenceError.
A trailing expression yields null (documented in the exec schema), so the SPEC's P2 form returns no value; only `return` does.
No docs-vs-code mismatch found on isolation: the docs' 'no ambient filesystem, networking, subprocess, environment, or module access' matched every probe.
